title: India’s import reliance exposes vulnerabilities beyond energy: Crisil
content:
India’s dependence on imported energy and industrial inputs leaves the economy exposed to global disruptions, with mining and manufacturing the most import-dependent major sectors. 
Crisil said diversification, strategic reserves and stronger domestic production are crucial to reduce supply shocks, inflation risks and reliance on critical imports.

title: ICE cotton notices mix trend amid consolidation phases
content:
ICE cotton futures consolidated after Wednesday’s surge, with December 2026 settling at 88.34 cents after testing 89.45 cents per pound. 
China’s State Reserve logged its 24th straight 100 per cent sold-out auction; USDA export sales reached 280,110 bales for the week ended August 13. 
US crop ratings fell to 38 per cent amid Texas heat and dryness, keeping support as December eyes 90 cents.

title: India expands rupee-based export rules to support international trade
content:
India has eased rupee-based export rules, allowing eligible exporters to invoice contracts in rupees or foreign currencies and receive payments through approved channels. 
Rupee-realised exports can qualify for FTP benefits and export-obligation fulfilment, while separate rules apply to ACU markets. 
The changes could reduce currency conversion costs and exchange-rate risks.

title: Indonesia’s 11.9% textile investment boom has a $2.3 bn problem
content:
Indonesia’s textile and apparel investment rose 11.85 per cent to IDR11.40 trillion in H1 2026, while sector growth reached 6.36 per cent in Q2.
TexPro shows a $2.29-billion HS50–60 upstream deficit in January–May, against a $3.25-billion apparel surplus.
Rising imports of fibres, fabrics, nonwovens and cotton show factories relying more on overseas inputs, led by China and Vietnam.

title: Bangladesh opens MSME registration for tax, business benefits
content:
Bangladesh’s SME Foundation opened online MSME registration; certificates follow verification and a Tk1,000 (~$8) fee. 
Registered SMEs can claim turnover-based tax exemptions; thresholds are higher for women and entrepreneurs with disabilities. 
Certificates enable annual overseas business remittances of up to $3,000 and access to fairs, export training, easier loans and matchmaking.
